सर्वाष् टीकाः
Gemini 3.8 Flash

He sacrifices to the Vājins;
the Vājins indeed are cattle;
them he sacrifices then.
This is not quite like a well-performed sacrifice;
for when the sacrifice has concluded and the enclosing-sticks have been thrown into the fire, he offers.

सर्वाष् टीकाः
Gemini 3.8 Flash

The hyenas indeed ate the ascetics.
Their heads are these date palms;
that which is the karīra shoots stretches up as the drinking of Soma.
In that there are karīra shoots,
he secures the drinking of Soma.
The mountains, indeed, are this eldest offspring of Prajāpati.
They were winged;
they flew away and settled wherever they wished.
Now this [earth] then was loose.
Indra cut off their wings;
with them he made this [earth] firm.
The wings that were [cut off] became clouds;
therefore they drift towards the mountain,
for that is their birthplace;
therefore it rains most abundantly on a mountain.
What trickled forth became those karīra shoots.
Therefore in the rainy season, when the clouds emerge, they float;

Gemini 3.8 Flash

Having created creatures and having sacrificed away distress, he desired: “May I slay Vṛtra.”
Having joined together with these deities—the Maruts as the folk, Agni as the vanguard—he advanced.
Having approached Vṛtra and having seen Vṛtra, he stood paralyzed in the thighs, not daring to attack.
The Maruts charged upon him with wind-chariots of reed;
they went over [him].
Where they reached his vital part, there he writhed;
then indeed they scorched him thoroughly;
therefore [these offerings are] the Sāṃtapanas.
The Sākamedhas are destroying Vṛtra.
With Agni as the vanguard, Indra slew Vṛtra,
precisely for having a vanguard.
This Agni is the commander of the gods’ army;
this [offering] is indeed for raising the army.
Indra could not raise the thunderbolt against Vṛtra;
he poured out this portion for the Maruts;
the Maruts scorched him thoroughly for heroic strength;

About to slay Vṛtra tomorrow, they fasted nearby.
They said: “To whom indeed will this [world] belong tomorrow? For whom will there be cooking?”
They cooked this boiled rice.
They looked out for the cattle: “Whichever of these two [sides] they shall favor tomorrow, they shall be the conquerors.”
With this [rice] they went forth towards them;
with this they held them;
this is the path of cattle.
They dwelt [there], victorious on the morrow.
They said: “To whom indeed will this [world] belong tomorrow? For whom will there be cooking?”
They cooked this boiled rice.
They said: “Let us not eat what has not been offered.”
They offered to the Maruts, the Gṛhamedhas;
the Maruts, the Gṛhamedhas, are cattle;
to them indeed they offered then.
They were arrayed for battle.
The Asuras sent hunger against the gods.
The gods, having heard it coming, cooked this boiled rice.
Not having found a place among the gods, it entered the Asuras again;
it burned them up.
Even in the vicinity, one should cook boiled rice;
